attempts.note: lamisplus.org is a WordPress marketing site; /v3/api-docs and every other well-known spec path return the same 3164-byte HTML page. docs.lamisplus.org and www.lamisplus.org do not resolve.

LAMISPlus modules DO configure Springfox (Docket, DocumentationType.SWAGGER_2, title 'Lamisplus'), and the v3 core ships a Redoc page at GET /redoc.html — so every running deployment serves its own machine spec at /v2/api-docs or /v3/api-docs. There is no public deployment to fetch it from: LAMISPlus is installed per facility behind a login, and the implementing partner's own test tooling records that '/swagger-ui/index.html and every api-docs path on QA answer 401 to an anonymous request, to a valid bearer token and to basic auth'. Anyone with instance credentials should re-capture this spec from their own /v3/api-docs and the origin becomes found-openapi.

The org holds the v2-era module sources; the v3 backend ('Lamisplus3.0/api') is not published.

notes: LAMISPlus is a self-hosted, open-source EMR used across Nigeria; there is no vendor API portal, no published machine spec, and no public instance, so this document is authored rather than captured. It describes LAMISPlus v3 — the version the adaptor targets, identifiable by the { statusCode, message, data } envelope the adaptor's getPatients reads (body.data.patients) — and covers 106 operations over 104 paths of the ~460 endpoints a v3 deployment exposes, which is why completeness is best-effort with reason partial-docs rather than complete. Every path here has evidence behind it: 83 come from the endpoint inventory the implementing partner generates from the real v3 backend source, ~25 more from the paths their API and UI tests call against a live instance, and the patient create/read-by-id pair from the vendor's own PatientController plus the adaptor's generic helpers. Two transcription bugs in the partner's generated inventory were corrected against the paths their hand-written tests actually call: '/plugin/ehrapi/v1/...' and '/plugin/inpatientapi/v1/...' are really '/plugin/ehr/api/v1/...' and '/plugin/inpatient/api/v1/...'. What is NOT covered: the ~350 remaining endpoints (all the POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH surface and every GET that needs a path variable), and the billing and sync plugins, which the partner's extractor skips because it has no mount prefix for them. Response bodies are modelled only where they were observed: 11 named data objects (Patient, User, UserSettings, Role, Plugin, ServicePoint, PagedResponse, ContentPage, PatientPage, ConsultationDashboard, LoginResponse). The rest carry an empty schema and a description saying the shape is not documented — deliberately, rather than inventing fields. This replaces an earlier synthesized spec whose eight endpoints were mostly 'plausible reconstructions'; its Patient schema constrained sex to an enum, uuid to format uuid and address to a string, all three contradicted by the vendor's Person entity (unconstrained String, plain String, jsonb) and all three the cause of the ten conformance violations the mocker was reporting. Finally: every deployment serves its own Springfox/Redoc spec behind the login (GET /redoc.html is in the core inventory), so anyone with instance credentials can turn this into a found-openapi capture.
